CLICK HERE)A historic season for the Miami RedHawks has come to an end.On Friday, the Miami men's basketball team was eliminated by Tennessee in a crushing 78-56 loss. This comes after the RedHawks had won their First Four game of the NCAA tournament just days before against Southern Methodist University, allowing the team to advance to the Round of 64.The RedHawks got off to an early lead against the Volunteers in the first four minutes of the game with a round of early three-point shots made shortly after tip-off.However, the Volunteers would quickly rally back, before going on to run away with the win.By halftime, the score was 51-32 in favor of Tennessee, with the Volunteers going on to extend their lead in the second half.Ja'Kobilespie led the way for Tennessee with 29 points. Following him were J.P. Estrella with 14 points and Felix Okpara with 12 points.Meanwhile, the RedHawks' leading scorer was Peter Suder, who put up nearly half of Miami's point total at 27 points.While Miami boasted seven different players who were averaging ten points or more during the regular season, only Suder would prove to be able to get into a shooting rhythm on Friday against Tennessee, with the rest of the team's roster only putting up point totals in the single digits.Despite the loss, it comes as Miami has cemented itself in NCAA history as one of just a very small handful of teams to go undefeated in their regular season.The loss to Tennessee is now the second to occur to the RedHawks in the postseason: Miami's first loss came last week as part of the MAC conference tournament, where the RedHawks fell to Massachusetts in a stunning 87-83 upset.Tennessee will now take on Virginia on Sunday.Meanwhile, the Miami women's team is set to face off against West Virginia in the first round of their own March Madness tournament on Saturday at 5 p.m. PHILADELPHIA — (Can't see the scoreboard above?
